title: Bison workspace provisioning · input
description: Body of POST /webhook/workspace-setup-bison, and the item passed to the executeWorkflowTrigger. Sent by the orm-gateway `requestWorkspaceSetup` action. Identical in shape to the Aimfox input except that workspace_id is a numeric string, not a UUID — the gateway must not assume one id format for both sequencers. The gateway never forwards a vendor credential: the master key lives only as an n8n credential (process doc, invariant 7).

client_id.description: public.clients.id. The workflow resolves the client name from it; the caller never supplies the name, so a renamed client cannot silently target a different workspace.

workspace_id.description: Bison workspace id — an integer the platform renders as a string ('73', '125'), NOT a UUID. When present it wins outright and no name search happens; this is how an operator answers a `needs_selection`. The old canvas had '13' — the Testing workspace — hardcoded into every URL, which is why it could serve exactly one client.

dry_run.description: true performs every read and no write, and returns the same `steps` object as a real run. This is what the portal's "Перевірити" button sends, and what feeds the status column.

requested_by.description: users.id of the internal user who pressed the button, or null when the run was triggered by client creation. Recorded in integration_sync_runs.metadata for audit — provisioning writes into a client's sending system, so who asked is part of the record.
